mechanism: Neither name is registered: nothing under src/wallet/ defines them, gethash on bl.rpc::*rpc-methods* answers NIL for both, and dispatch-rpc-method takes its unknown-method branch (src/rpc/server.lisp:79-82) and signals -32601 "Method not found". Their argument rows exist in src/rpc/core-tables.lisp:294 and :322 only because that table is generated from Core. Core registers both in the wallet command table (refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/rpc/wallet.cpp:929, :945) and implements them in rpc/backup.cpp:39-93 and :94-127. Neither is legacy-only: importprunedfunds decodes a raw transaction plus a gettxoutproof CMerkleBlock, checks ExtractMatches against the header's merkle root, resolves the block through findAncestorByHash, and calls AddToWallet with TxStateConfirmed; removeprunedfunds calls CWallet::RemoveTxs (wallet.cpp:2419-2470), which erases the tx rows inside a db transaction and unwinds mapWallet / wtxOrdered / mapTxSpends / m_txos on commit. Both operate on descriptor wallets -- d3056bc can no longer create a legacy wallet at all. The prerequisites we already ship: gettxoutproof, verifytxoutproof and abandontransaction are all in the method table, and -prune is a supported option (src/config-options.lisp:56). What is missing on our side beyond the two handlers is the RemoveTxs primitive: grep finds no remove-txs / erase-tx equivalent anywhere in src/wallet/.
consequence: A pruned node -- a configuration we support -- cannot add a known transaction to a wallet whose blocks are no longer on disk, and no wallet can delete a transaction record at all. Two Core functional tests exercise the pair (wallet_importprunedfunds.py in full, and wallet_resendwallettransactions.py:88-116 which uses removeprunedfunds to drop a replaced child), so both are unrunnable against us. This is an absent capability answered with an honest "Method not found", not a wrong answer, so S3. The scoping question resolves against the finding's own doubt: docs/wallet-plan.md scopes out migratewallet, BIP39 and external signers and says nothing about these two, and docs/next-wave-2026-08-22.md:336-338 sizes them as planned S-sized work. The one document that appears to exclude them, docs/coverage-vs-core-2026-08-24.md:35, files them under "Legacy BDB wallet (excluded by design)" -- a misclassification, since backup.cpp's implementations touch no legacy code -- and its own next sentence (:40) contradicts the table by calling them "genuinely missing". So this is not a recorded scoping with its consequence stated; it is a gap with a wrong label on it.

Core at d3056bc: wallet/rpc/backup.cpp:39-127, wallet/rpc/wallet.cpp:929,945, wallet/wallet.cpp:2419-2470 (RemoveTxs), test/functional/wallet_importprunedfunds.py (registered in test_runner.py:273) and wallet_resendwallettransactions.py:116.
fix_shape: Port both handlers as a pair into src/wallet/wallet-tx.lisp beside the other wallet/rpc/transactions.cpp ports. importprunedfunds: decode the raw transaction (Core's -22 "TX decode failed. Make sure the tx has at least one input."), parse the second argument as a merkle block with the existing verifytxoutproof codec, require ExtractMatches to reproduce the header's merkle root (-5 "Something wrong with merkleblock"), resolve the header hash to a block-index entry that is an ancestor of the wallet's last block (-5 "Block not found in chain"), require the transaction to appear in the proof (-5 "Transaction given doesn't exist in proof"), and only then call wallet-add-to-wallet with a confirmed state carrying the block hash, height and the index the proof gives; when nothing in the wallet is mine, signal -5 "No addresses in wallet correspond to included transaction". removeprunedfunds needs the missing primitive first: a wallet-remove-txs mirroring CWallet::RemoveTxs -- refuse with -4 "Transaction <txid> does not belong to this wallet" for an unknown id, erase the tx record, and unwind the in-memory maps (map-wallet, the ordered list, the spends index, the TXO map) only once the write has landed, since Core does that work in the db transaction's on_commit listener. Take wallet_importprunedfunds.py as the acceptance oracle, including its conflicting-transaction case at :133-154.
